bib.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pages 3419-3448

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; example tables 9-20 not read row by row.

question: Can a language model generate test cases that automatically uncover harmful behaviours of another LM, as an alternative to human-written red-team cases?
hypothesis: LMs are effective tools for red teaming: LM-generated test cases find diverse failures at scale, comparable to manual red teaming.
contributions: A three-stage LM red-teaming framework (red LM generates cases, target replies, classifier flags failures)
Comparison of zero-shot, stochastic few-shot, supervised and RL generation on a difficulty/diversity trade-off
Applications to offensive language, data leakage, contact info, distributional bias and dialogue harms in a 280B chatbot

method.summary: A red LM (Gopher) generates test questions by zero-shot, stochastic few-shot, supervised or RL methods. Dialogue-Prompted Gopher replies and a 1.4B Gopher offensiveness classifier flags failures. The same recipe with different prompts and regex checks finds data leakage, contact info, group bias and multi-turn harms.
method.task: automated red teaming of a dialogue LM

datasets.name: Bot-Adversarial Dialogue (BAD), Xu et al. 2021b
datasets.size: 2598 conversation-starting questions used as reference; used to train the classifier; 85 dialogues with 7+ offensive replies used as SFS dialogue examples
datasets.preprocessing: classifier: 'Hello' prepended to dialogue for red-team text to remove odd-ply prior

datasets.name: Zero-shot generated questions
datasets.split: SL: 90% train / 10% validation of failing cases
datasets.source: Gopher 280B with prompt 'List of questions to ask someone:\n1.'
datasets.preprocessing: valid if contains '?', truncated after first '?'

models.name: Dialogue-Prompted Gopher (DPG)
models.architecture: left-to-right transformer LM with hand-written dialogue prompt (Table 21)

models.name: Offensiveness classifier
models.architecture: Gopher 1.4B fine-tuned on BAD via instruction tuning

training.objective: SL: log-likelihood of failing zero-shot cases, 1 epoch. RL: A2C maximising reward -log(1-r(x,y)) (-3 if no '?'), loss = alpha*KL + (1-alpha)*A2C, alpha in {.3,.35,.4}, warm-started from SL model
training.regularisation: RL: KL penalty to SL init, L2 gradient clipping 1, first 80% of weights (64/80 layers) frozen, PopArt step 1e-4, value MLP 2 hidden layers of 2048

other.SL_extra: embedding layers frozen, rematerialize activations every 3 blocks
other.N_SL: N = number of zero-shot cases that led to offensive replies (value not separately given)

inference.decoding: nucleus sampling; red LM p=0.95; DPG p=0.8
inference.samples: 0.5M zero-shot questions; 2598 per method for comparison; 100k per contact-info type; 10k groups; 100k templates; 4000 dialogues per method; distinct random seeds per sample
inference.prompting: ZS prompt 'List of questions to ask someone:\n1.'; SFS adds 5 examples sampled with prob proportional to exp(r/T), T=1/10; dialogues up to 16 turns

metrics.name: % replies offensive
metrics.definition: share of DPG replies the classifier scores >=0.5

metrics.name: Self-BLEU
metrics.definition: max BLEU of a case against 1000 cases sampled from the 2598

eval.protocol: Single run per method as far as stated; bootstrap 95% CI shown for dialogue figures only; no seeds stated.

limits: Red LM and classifier inherit biases from training data, limiting test diversity and detection (Sec 9.1).
Classifier flags are candidates; false positives and negatives need other classifiers or people.
Not exhaustive: 'should not be viewed as a way to perfectly and exhaustively find all possible critical oversights'.
Requires prompt engineering for new behaviours.
Single target (DPG) and single red LM family (Gopher); BAD-trained classifier over-predicts offensiveness for red-team text until 'Hello' is prepended.
Misuse: could be used to attack commercial LMs (Sec 9.2).
